articles.title: Jedd Fisch Remains Noncommittal on Quarterback Decision
articles.summary: The third-year Washington Huskies head coach didn't offer a decision on whether Elijah Brown or Demond Williams Jr. will be the team's starter going forward.
articles.body:
The Washington Huskies offense showed sustained signs of life against a Big Ten opponent for the first time this season against the Purdue Boilermakers on Friday.

Third-year quarterback Elijah Brown made his first start since transferring to Washington from the Stanford Cardinal this offseason in place of injured third-year signal-caller Demond Williams Jr.

Brown had a mixed bag in his first UW start, but still was able to guide the team to victory. He went 21-for-27 for 302 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. With Brown under center, Washington (4-3 overall, 1-3 in Big Ten play) won its first Big Ten game of the season against Purdue, a 38-26 result , and scored more than 24 points against a Football Bowl Subdivision (FBS) opponent for the first time this year.

Williams was available in pads on the sidelines in an emergency quarterback scenario.

The Huskies will have a much-needed bye week this week and will next be in action on the road against the Nebraska Cornhuskers at a to-be-determined time Oct. 31 (Halloween) in Lincon, Neb.

Despite Washington having its best overall performance as an offense this season, aside from a 48-16 win against the Eastern Washington Eagles of the Football Championship Subdivision (FCS), head coach Jedd Fisch was noncommittal about which quarterback will start against Nebraska.

"No we're not going to make any assumptions like that," Fisch said after the game, according to a post on "X" shared by Dave Mahler. "We're going to enjoy tonight and then we'll be coaches on Sunday."

In six starts this season (five of which were full games), Williams has completed 66.7% of his passes for 1,396 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions and a quarterback rating (QBR) of 41.3, which ranks 105th in the country. He's added another 183 yards and two touchdowns on the ground on 64 runs.

In three appearances (one start), Brown has completed 73.9% of his passes for 578 yards, seven touchdowns and three interceptions and has a QBR of 73.8.

In Brown's three halves over the last two weeks at the helm of the team, the Huskies offense has scored 59 points.

In two-and-a-half Big Ten games (five halves), Williams has led the Washington offense to 48 points.

The Huskies have five more games left on their schedule: the one against Nebraska, one against the Penn State Nittany Lions at home Nov. 7, another on the road against the Michigan State Spartans on Nov. 14, another at home against the No. 5 Indiana Hoosiers on Nov. 21 and UW will wrap up the season on the road against the Oregon Ducks on Nov. 28. Washington will need to win two more games in that slate to be bowl-eligible.

articles.title: 'Short ball again': Babar Azam misses out on 50 as Sri Lanka exploit Pakistan star's weakness in Tri-series opener
articles.summary: Fans erupted in disdain as Babar Azam once again got dismissed before scoring his fifty, this time with a short ball, and supporters weren't ready to let thi...
articles.body:
Babar Azam was dismissed for 45 off 57 balls by a short ball as Pakistan batted first against Sri Lanka in the tri-series opener.

Sri Lanka won the toss and chose to bowl first at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium.

Fans on X criticised the way Babar handled the short ball and questioned how he would cope against stronger attacks.

Babar Azam falls short of a fifty in the tri-series opener vs Sri Lanka

Babar Azam missed out on a half-century in Pakistan's opening match of the ODI tri-series against Sri Lanka at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Sunday, October 18. Pakistan were asked to bat first after Sri Lanka won the toss and chose to bowl.

Babar, who was listed at No. 3 in Pakistan's lineup, was dismissed for 45 off 57 balls by a short ball, leaving him five runs short of a fifty. The wicket has come at a tough point for the hosts.

This match is the first of six league games in the tri-series between Pakistan, England and Sri Lanka, with the top two teams moving into the final at Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore on October 31.

All three nations are using the series to prepare for the 2027 World Cup. With Babar seen as Pakistan's top batter and their main anchor, his inability to hold his wicket and convert milestones has been the topic of much scrutiny from the cricketing world. Fans on X even took shots at his record against the short ball.

Fans react to Babar Azam's dismissal as Sri Lanka exploit Pakistan star's weakness

Babar was already under scrutiny after Pakistan's 3-0 Test whitewash in England, where he fell to a Jofra Archer bouncer at Lord's, so another short-ball dismissal drew an instant reaction. One fan wrote , "NO WAAAAY! Babar Azam gets dismissed by a short ball AGAIN! He departs for 45 off 57 balls. 💔"

Another fan also took aim at his scoring rate, noting that Babar's 45 came at a strike rate of around 79, and compared him with Indian batter Shreyas Iyer. They wrote , "India has Shreyas Iyer. Pakistan has Babar azam. Both are mug against short balls; both do tuk-tuk on flat pitch. both fail on tough wickets So many similarities, man 😭."

The surface was part of the discussion too, with Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis having called it "a great batting track" at the toss. A third fan felt the bounce on offer had made the difference and wrote, "Babar going with the short ball, soft dismissal as both Fakhar and Babar have shown that this pitch helps hitting the deck hard."

Some supporters tied the wicket to his struggles in England, where Babar made 8 and 6 at Lord's and was then bowled for 7 at Edgbaston. One fan went further and wrote, "Babar Azam dismissed for 45. Babar Azam can't play short balls. Since Jofra Archer's short ball, everyone is exploiting this weakness."

The next big test is not far away, as Pakistan face England in Rawalpindi on October 20, although Archer has been rested from England's squad for the series. A final fan questioned what the dismissal meant for tougher assignments and wrote, "Babar Needs to work on his Short Ball issues. If these ordinary bowlers are dismissing him on the short ball, how will he survive against the top quality bowlers?"

Babar Azam must solve his short-ball problem before the 2027 World Cup

Babar Azam's short-ball problem is now as much about shot selection as technique. He had faced 57 balls, played a few fine drives and helped steady Pakistan after two powerplay wickets, yet he pulled a short ball from Eshan Malinga in the 20th over straight to a fielder.

Nothing forced the shot. Pakistan were batting first, a long way from any chase, and his strike rate of around 79 was below his career rate of roughly 87. A batter with 20 ODI hundreds and an average above 53 did not need to take on that ball.

Sri Lanka have also handed every other attack a template. England are in Rawalpindi on October 20 and will plan around the same length, so Babar needs a clear method, whether that is leaving it, ducking it or pulling only when he is set up for it, rather than another instinctive swing.

To keep up to date with all the latest cricket news and share your opinion on the biggest topics, visit our Facebook , Instagram and X (Twitter) pages.

articles.title: Liverpool star shines against Brentford but leaves Iraola with issue
articles.summary: Florian Wirtz Remains Liverpool’s Big Tactical Question After Brentford WinLiverpool got the result they needed at Brentford. They responded to a first leagu...
articles.body:
Florian Wirtz Remains Liverpool's Big Tactical Question After Brentford Win

Liverpool got the result they needed at Brentford. They responded to a first league defeat of the season, collected an away win and climbed to fifth. On the surface, that is the kind of afternoon Andoni Iraola would have taken without much fuss. Dig a little deeper, though, and the same question keeps coming back, what exactly is Liverpool's best shape with Florian Wirtz in it?

That is the issue raised in the original reporting by BBC Football, and it is hard to argue with the central point. Wirtz was productive, influential and statistically excellent in west London, yet he also remained at the centre of Liverpool's structural uncertainty.

The numbers were impressive. Wirtz created nine chances from open play, a standout figure by any measure and one that underlines why Liverpool committed a club record £116m to sign him from Bayer Leverkusen in June 2025. He was heavily involved in the attacking phase, drove Liverpool forward and helped initiate the comeback after Brentford were reduced to 10 men before half-time.

That part is easy to see. Wirtz gives you craft, imagination and final-third quality. He spots passes others do not. He plays on the half-turn, receives in pockets and increases the volume of dangerous actions around the box. Against Brentford, he recorded 12 final-third entries and 37 passes in the final third. Liverpool spent long stretches with him at the heart of their attacking work.

There is, however, another side to it, and this is where Liverpool's tactical balance becomes a serious conversation rather than a passing talking point. Wirtz lost possession 19 times, more than every Liverpool player apart from Milos Kerkez, and won only one of his nine duels. Those details matter because they feed directly into the wider concern about how open Liverpool can look when he plays as a number 10 in a side already using two wingers high and wide.

Liverpool tactical balance still looks unresolved

This is not really about whether Wirtz is talented enough. He plainly is. It is about what happens around him. If Liverpool play with Wirtz behind the striker, then a heavy burden falls on the deeper midfielders. They are asked to cover too much ground, close too many spaces and put out too many fires in transition. Against Brentford, even with the extra man, there were periods when Liverpool looked vulnerable in midfield and too easy to progress through.

Danny Murphy put it bluntly: "They got the job done. First and foremost, that's another win on the road, which is always positive," before adding, "But I thought they looked too easy to play against. The spaces are too big." He then got to the heart of it: "They're playing with two wingers and Wirtz at 10, so they're relying heavily on the two midfield players to try and cover so much space."

That sounds harsh, but it also sounds accurate. A side can create plenty and still be unstable. A side can win and still leave you unconvinced. Liverpool did both at Brentford.

This is where Iraola earns his keep. Good coaches do not merely fit stars into a shape and hope for the best. They build an environment in which the team functions with and without the ball. Right now, Liverpool look as though they are still searching for that equilibrium. Murphy's warning was straightforward: "It was too easy for Brentford to play out and to get in behind. That would be the biggest concern today for me."

Florian Wirtz production offers encouragement

For all the tactical debate, there are signs that Wirtz is beginning to affect games more consistently. He has now assisted in back-to-back matches in all competitions for the first time for Liverpool, and no player has created more Premier League chances this season. He is level on 18 with Brighton's Pascal Gross, which says plenty about his creative output even in a side that has yet to fully settle.

That matters because criticism of Wirtz had started to grow. Steven Gerrard had suggested earlier in the week that taking him out of the side might help restore confidence. After this display, that line of argument looks less persuasive. Liverpool do not have many players capable of producing this amount of invention from central areas. Remove him and you probably gain some control, but you also lose a significant share of your unpredictability.

Murphy's solution was clear enough: "They don't look solid and don't look together in terms of shape," and, "Instead of a number 10, where Wirtz is struggling to impact games, put three midfielders in." He also added, "Always, the priority is foundation, defence, stability, being hard to beat. The other stuff can follow from there."

That is a legitimate football argument. It is also a conservative one. Iraola may decide that the upside of Wirtz's creativity is worth the trade-off, particularly if Liverpool can improve their rest defence, pressing distances and protection in front of the back line. Systems are rarely fixed in September or October. They evolve.

The timing is awkward. Liverpool are trying to establish a new identity under a new head coach while the schedule begins to bite. Alexander Isak returned from injury, which is a major boost, but Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong both picked up injuries at Brentford. That leaves Iraola with less room for experimentation at the very point when he needs options.

The manager acknowledged the strain afterwards, saying: "When you come here, you see the results of Brentford at home and you have to be ready for this kind of battle." He also said: "We had a lot of chances. Even at the end, we had some counters where we were three against one and need to finish. When we go 2-1, every throw-in and every free-kick can be a problem."

More revealing was his assessment of the wider picture: "We are in a delicate situation with some of the players. We were talking about this run of four games in 10 days, it's very, very demanding." Looking ahead, he added: "We have to rest again because we have another big, big game against Villarreal [in the Champions League on Tuesday]."

That probably tells you everything. Liverpool have won, Wirtz has delivered and the fixture list keeps moving. Yet the conundrum remains. Wirtz can elevate Liverpool's attack, but if the collective structure around him remains loose, stronger opponents will punish it. Iraola has a gifted playmaker on his hands. He also has a tactical problem to solve.

From a hopeful Liverpool perspective, there is still plenty to like here. Wirtz is clearly a top-level footballer, and supporters can see that every time he gets on the ball in dangerous areas. Players who create nine chances in a Premier League match do not grow on trees. If he is doing that while still settling into a new league, under a new coach, in a side that has not fully clicked, there is obvious reason for optimism.

The bigger point is that this feels fixable. Tactical balance can be coached. Distances between midfield and attack can be tightened. Full-backs can be managed differently. One midfielder can sit a little deeper. None of that requires tearing up the plan.

Iraola has inherited a squad that still looks like a work in progress, and injuries are already complicating things. Even so, wins like this matter because they buy time. Liverpool do not need panic or overreaction after seven league games. They need patience and a few practical adjustments.

If Wirtz keeps producing creatively and Isak stays fit, the attacking quality is there for a strong season. The challenge is to make the side harder to play through without blunting its best weapon. Get that right, and this conversation shifts very quickly from conundrum to catalyst.

articles.title: Former Nebraska QB Dylan Raiola comes off bench in fourth quarter to lead Oregon to 17-14 win over the Cornhuskers
articles.summary: Raiola spent the first two years of his college career at Nebraska before transferring in the offseason but was benched ahead of Saturday night's game.
articles.body:
Dylan Raiola got the chance to beat his former team after all.

The Oregon quarterback came off the bench in the second half and threw the game-winning touchdown pass with 28 seconds to go as the Ducks beat Nebraska 17-14.

Raiola found tight end Jamari Johnson for the go-ahead score from four yards away. Nebraska made it 35 yards in five plays after the TD, but wasn't able to get into position for a game-tying field goal.

The junior quarterback replaced Brock Thomas in the fourth quarter after Thomas threw an interception on Oregon's final drive of the third quarter. Thomas' pick came as Oregon trailed 7-6, and Nebraska turned the interception into a touchdown six plays later.

"So we made the decision to go ahead and make a [QB] change," Oregon coach Dan Lanning said in his postgame news conference. "And I went over to Brock and told him 'hey, we're going to try to create a spark for our guys and want to make a change here. But it's not necessarily anything you did, just we need to do something different, right? We're not going to keep doing the same thing.' And Brock said I completely understand coach, and love you and I want to do whatever's best for the team and I just think that shows so much remarkable courage from a guy like that, to be in that situation.

"And it's got to be disappointing in that moment to be like, hey, I'm good with it. Let's do whatever we've got to do to win."

Raiola immediately led Oregon to a field goal on a drive that took nearly half the fourth quarter as the Ducks ran 17 plays to go 69 yards. After Nebraska punted, Oregon then had a five-minute drive that went 82 yards. Raiola's pass to Johnson was the 20th play of the drive and Oregon's 37th play of the final quarter.

Thomas started the game after taking over for Raiola in Oregon's Week 6 loss to UCLA. Oregon turned the ball over seven times in that 17-15 loss to the Bruins and tumbled out of the AP Top 25 as a result.

Saturday night, Thomas was 9-of-20 passing for 54 yards and an interception. Raiola was 11-of-18 passing for 59 yards. He and Thomas combined to average three yards an attempt on their 38 throws.

Raiola transferred to Oregon after spending two seasons as Nebraska's starting quarterback. With Dante Moore's return to the Ducks for the 2026 season, Raiola entered the season as Moore's backup with the goal of taking over as the team's starter in 2027.

Raiola's first start in an Oregon uniform came much earlier than expected. Moore suffered a scary concussion in Oregon's Week 4 win over USC and has missed the Ducks' last two games.

The win moved Oregon to 4-2 ahead of a trip to Illinois in Week 8. Nebraska is now 5-2 overall after back-to-back losses and is off in Week 8 before hosting Washington on Halloween.

articles.title: 'SuperLópez' construye otro registro espectacular
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Juvenil A mantiene al equipo imbatido: ocho partidos y 720 minutos sin encajar un gol
articles.summary: El técnico del Juvenil A mantiene al equipo imbatido: ocho partidos y 720 minutos sin encajar un gol
articles.body: Álvaro López no para de sorprender en La Fábrica, donde hace tiempo que se le conoce como 'SuperLópez'. Un apodo más que justificado a tenor de los espectaculares logros que está firmando el técnico en las últimas temporadas. Álvaro López encadenó 45 victorias seguidas en Liga entre las temporadas 24-25 y 25-26, firmó un comienzo de Liga con 15 triunfos seguidos el pasado año con el Juvenil C y ha ganado cuatro títulos en nueve meses con el Juvenil A: Liga, Youth, Copa de Campeones e Intercontinental sub 20. El nuevo logro para la colección de la gran sensación de los banquillos en La Fábrica es una racha de imbatibilidad de ocho partidos y 720 minutos (más todos los minutos de prolongación) sin encajar un gol. El Juvenil A del Madrid lleva ocho partidos en lo que va de temporada (sin contar el partido de la Intercontinental, que lo disputó un equipo sub 20 que nada tiene que ver con el tercer filial blanco), seis de Liga y dos de Youth League, y en ninguno de ellos ha encajado un gol. Una fortaleza defensiva que, unido al descomunal talento ofensivo del equipo, le permite acumular un 22-0 en la diferencia de goles a favor y en contra y un balance de resultados de siete victorias y un empate. Una racha de imbatibilidad en la que han participado los dos porteros de la plantilla, Guille Ponce y Álvaro Rodríguez, y un total de 11 defensas: Bailón, Ares, Luis Paulo, Alejandro Castaño, Espinosa, Guille, Joan Martínez, Mateo Garrido, Lezcano, Lemaitre y Mario Rivas.
